topics.name: SAM Overview & Fundamentals
topics.description: Software asset management basics, process architecture, and recommended practices.

introduction.overview: SAM Fundamentals covers the core concepts of Software Asset Management in ServiceNow, including the business drivers for SAM, the SAM process architecture, and implementation best practices for successful deployments.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 14% of the CIS-SAM exam. Questions cover SAM business value, license compliance drivers, the SAM solution architecture, implementation methodology, and best practices for SAM rollouts.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand why organizations need SAM (compliance, cost optimization, risk reduction). Know the SAM solution architecture including SAM Pro vs SAM. Master the recommended implementation sequence and stakeholder engagement strategies.
introduction.examTips: SAM helps organizations avoid audit penalties and optimize license spending. Know the difference between SAM (foundation) and SAM Pro (advanced features). Implementation should start with high-risk publishers first.

topics.name: Data Integrity & Sources
topics.description: Importing data, software discovery, normalization, and content services.

introduction.overview: Data Integrity covers how software data flows into ServiceNow SAM, including discovery methods, data import processes, normalization to create accurate software models, and how Content Services enriches the data.
introduction.whyItMatters: Data Integrity is 28% of the exam. Expect questions on Discovery integration, software import processes, Normalization Data Services, the Software Asset Model Library, and how to ensure data quality for accurate compliance reporting.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master the data flow from Discovery to SAM. Understand how normalization matches discovered software to software models. Know how Content Services provides publisher-specific license metrics and entitlement rules.
introduction.examTips: Discovery provides raw software data; normalization creates clean models. The Software Asset Model Library contains certified software definitions. Content Services adds license metric knowledge for compliance calculations.

topics.name: Software Compliance Management
topics.description: Products and models, license metrics, entitlements, allocations, and software reconciliation.

introduction.overview: Software Compliance is the heart of SAM, covering how to define license entitlements, measure software usage, allocate licenses to users or devices, and reconcile entitlements against installations for compliance reporting.
introduction.whyItMatters: This is the largest domain at 30% of the exam. Questions focus on software products and models, license metric types (per device, per user, per core), entitlement creation, allocation strategies, and the reconciliation process.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the software model hierarchy (publisher > product > version > edition). Master license metric types and when each applies. Know how to create entitlements from contracts and allocate them. Understand reconciliation rules for compliance calculations.
introduction.examTips: Different publishers use different license metrics. Entitlements define what you own; allocations assign those rights. Reconciliation compares entitlements vs installations. Know how to interpret compliance status (compliant, non-compliant, over-licensed).

keyConcepts: Per device vs per user licensing

topics.name: Operational Integration
topics.description: Contract and change management, service catalog, procurement, and software remediation.

introduction.overview: Operational Integration covers how SAM connects with other ServiceNow modules and business processes, including contract management for license tracking, procurement workflows, service catalog for software requests, and remediation for compliance issues.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 13% of the exam. Questions cover software contract management, procurement integration, service catalog items for software requests, change management for software deployments, and remediation workflows for non-compliance.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand how contracts feed entitlements. Know how procurement workflows automate license purchases. Master service catalog integration for self-service software requests. Understand remediation options (reclaim, uninstall, purchase) for compliance issues.
introduction.examTips: Contracts are the source of truth for entitlements. Procurement can automatically create entitlements from purchase orders. Service catalog requests should check license availability. Remediation workflows help resolve non-compliance.

topics.name: Extending SAM
topics.description: Software model lifecycle, retirement, installation optimization, reporting, and maintenance.

introduction.overview: Extending SAM covers advanced capabilities including managing the software model lifecycle, optimizing installations to reduce costs, retirement workflows for end-of-life software, and reporting strategies for stakeholder communication.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 15% of the exam. Questions focus on software lifecycle management, end-of-life and end-of-support tracking, license optimization strategies, SAM dashboards and reports, and ongoing maintenance tasks.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master software lifecycle states and transitions. Understand end-of-life and end-of-support implications. Know license optimization techniques (harvesting, right-sizing). Understand SAM reports and dashboards for different audiences.
introduction.examTips: End-of-life software poses security risks. License optimization can significantly reduce costs. SAM dashboards should be tailored to the audience (executives vs SAM analysts). Regular maintenance keeps SAM data accurate.
